title: Is the land getting drier in Iowa?
subtitle: Root-zone soil wetness in the growing season, 1981-2025

variable.name: Root-zone soil wetness
variable.definition: How full of water the soil is in the layer where plant roots grow, as a fraction of saturation. Important for crops and drought.
variable.caveat: Modelled, not measured directly: reanalysis soil wetness depends on the land model and the rainfall it is fed. Irrigation and drainage are not fully represented.
variable.source: NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis, accessed via NASA POWER

raw.method: Mann-Kendall + Sen's slope on raw monthly values (ignores seasons & autocorrelation)
raw.plain: Growing-season soil wetness fell by about 0.00579 fraction (0 = dry, 1 = saturated) per decade (95% CI -0.0111 to -0.00056), p = 0.028: statistically significant.

deseasonalized.method: Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall + Sen's slope on monthly anomalies
deseasonalized.plain: Growing-season soil wetness: estimated change -0.00742 fraction (0 = dry, 1 = saturated) per decade (95% CI -0.0159 to 0.00122), p = 0.09. Not statistically significant - this does not prove there is no trend; a longer record might settle it.

seasonal_mk.method: Seasonal Mann-Kendall (each calendar month tested separately, then pooled) + Sen's slope
seasonal_mk.plain: Growing-season soil wetness fell by about 0.00817 fraction (0 = dry, 1 = saturated) per decade (95% CI -0.0121 to -0.00401), p = 0.000: statistically significant.

season_only.method: Mann-Kendall + Sen's slope on yearly June-August (growing season) means
season_only.plain: Growing-season soil wetness: estimated change -0.00741 fraction (0 = dry, 1 = saturated) per decade (95% CI -0.0195 to 0.00838), p = 0.30. Not statistically significant - this does not prove there is no trend; a longer record might settle it.

metrics.verdict_text: Whether the trend looks real depends on which years you pick: its size, direction or significance changes between periods. Treat any single-period result with caution, and check which years or events drive it.

notes: Regional value = average of 9 MERRA-2 grid cells inside the region (about 0.5 x 0.6 degrees each).
Reanalysis data blend a weather model with satellite and ground observations; trends can be affected by changes in the observing system.
Heatmap windows overlap heavily, so it is a descriptive sensitivity view, not many independent tests.
'Not significant' does not mean 'no trend' - a longer record may be needed.
